nodes.source_text: we prepared experimentally a suite of Cu-Al model catalysts: ion-implanted Al-on-Cu and evaporated-and-etched Al-on-Cu (see Methods and Supplementary Fig. 4)

nodes.name: Evaporation and etching Al-on-Cu
nodes.procedure: Evaporated-and-etched Al-on-Cu catalyst was prepared (see Methods and Supplementary Fig. 4).

nodes.name: Thermal evaporation and dealloying
nodes.procedure: Thermal evaporation and co-sputtering followed by chemical etching to synthesize de-alloyed nanoporous Cu-Al catalysts (Supplementary Information).
nodes.source_text: We explored both thermal evaporation and co-sputtering followed by chemical etching to synthesize de-alloyed nanoporous Cu-Al catalysts

nodes.name: Nanoporous Cu control synthesis
nodes.procedure: Control catalysts—nanoporous Cu on C-GDL with a very low amount of Al on the surface and having similar nanoporosity to that of the de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst (see Methods, Supplementary Information and Supplementary Figs. 35–36).
nodes.source_text: We further designed control catalysts—nanoporous Cu on C-GDL with a very low amount of Al on the surface and having similar nanoporosity to that of the de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst

nodes.name: Cu-Al on PTFE with carbon coating
nodes.procedure: Carbon nanoparticles/graphite were coated on the de-alloyed Cu-Al surface to create a sandwich structure that would distribute the current uniformly over the catalyst to stabilize its surface during reaction.
nodes.source_text: we fabricated de-alloyed Cu-Al catalysts on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) substrates... Carbon nanoparticles/graphite were coated on the de-alloyed Cu-Al surface

nodes.description: CO2 electroreduction on C-GDL in 1 M KOH flow-cell at 600 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: we achieved C₂H₄ Faradaic efficiency of 80% at a current density of 600 mA cm⁻²... Overall C₂₊ (multi-carbon product) production Faradaic efficiency was 85-90%... A CO₂-to-C₂H₄ half-cell power conversion efficiency (PCE)... of 34% was achieved... An average C₂H₄ Faradaic efficiency of 75 ± 4% was obtained over 17 de-alloyed distinct Cu-Al on C-GDL samples

nodes.description: CO2 electroreduction on PTFE in 1 M KOH at 400 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: we achieved C₂H₄ Faradaic efficiencies over 80% in 1 M KOH at a current density of 400 mA cm⁻²... The Cu-Al on C-GDL catalysts exhibited stable potentials between −1.8 V and −2.1 V versus RHE and a C₂H₄ Faradaic efficiency of 75% over 5 h... We demonstrated over 100 h of stability at this best condition

nodes.description: CO2 electroreduction on PTFE in 3 M KOH + 3 M KI at 150 mA/cm²
nodes.source_text: 3 M KOH (pH 14.5) allowed us to reach 48-52% half-cell C₂H₄ PCE at a current density of 150 mA cm⁻²... adding an additional 3 M KI into the electrolyte... This further diminished the CO Faradaic efficiency to below 0.3% and reduced H₂ production by 3%, increasing the C₂H₄ Faradaic efficiency to 73 ± 4%. As a result, we achieved a 55 ± 2% half-cell C₂H₄ PCE... This energy conversion efficiency was stable over 50 h

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanoporous structure with pore sizes of 5–20 nm for de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst before and after CO2 electroreduction; grain size increased after reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in SEM and high-angle angular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 21), a nanoporous structure with pore sizes of 5–20 nm was formed. After 5 h of CO2 electroreduction at a current density of 600 mA cm−2, the grain size increased...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals Cu (111) and (200) facets with interplanar spacings of 0.211 nm and 0.182 nm in de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We performed HAADF-STEM analysis and found that Cu (111) and (200) facets were observed with interplanar spacings of 0.211 nm and 0.182 nm (Supplementary Fig. 26).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS spectra (curves 1,2,3) at different areas of HAADF-STEM image confirm Al, Al2O3, CuO, Cu2O and Cu in de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst; homogeneous distribution before and after reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Curves numbered 1, 2 and 3 in the EELS spectra represent the EELS results measured at areas 1, 2 and 3 in the corresponding HAADF-STEM image. Al, Al2O3, CuO, Cu2O and Cu EELS results are plotted as references.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface Al concentrations: 4.5% (ion-implanted Al-on-Cu), 25% (evaporated-and-etched Al-on-Cu), 9% (de-alloyed Cu-Al after reaction), top 1-3 nm depth over 100 μm² area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To estimate quantitatively the amount of Al incorporated near the Cu surface, we used surface-sensitive Auger electron spectroscopic analysis... molar concentrations of Al on surfaces are 4.5% and 25% for the ion-implanted and evaporated-and-etched Al-on-Cu, respectively... Auger electron spectroscopic analysis revealed about 9% Al on the surface following the reaction (Supplementary Figs. 27 and 28).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ synchrotron XANES shows Cu-O bonding in de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst before, during, and after reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To investigate the Cu-Al catalyst further, we performed in situ synchrotron X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis... Cu-O bonding was observed via both ex situ and in situ XANES analyses with the de-alloyed Cu-Al catalyst before, during and after the reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) in TEM and SEM confirms homogeneous Al and Cu distribution in de-alloyed catalysts before and after 5 h reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analyses in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and SEM... indicated a homogeneous distribution of Al and Cu in de-alloyed catalysts before and also after 5 h of reaction (Fig. 2c and Supplementary Figs. 22–25).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows no obvious leaching of Al and Cu into solution during CO2 electrolysis; detected levels match KOH impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No obvious leaching of Al and Cu into the solution was observed via inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) analysis (Supplementary Fig. 44).
